back: Software that provides the services the computer needs to run and manage its hardware: operating system, utilities, device drivers and translators.
Software that provides the services the user needs to carry out a task, e.g. word processor, spreadsheet, browser, accounting package.
System software that performs one maintenance task to keep the computer secure, organised or efficient (anti-virus, backup, clean-up, defragmenter).
A program that lets the operating system communicate with a particular hardware device, such as a printer or webcam.

front: What does a disk defragmenter do?
back: Moves the parts (fragments) of each file on a magnetic hard disk so they are stored in one continuous area; the heads move less, so files open faster.
notes: It frees no space; not needed on an SSD.

back: Clean-up deletes unwanted files (temporary files, recycle bin) to free space; compression makes kept files smaller.
Scans files and compares them with a database of known malware signatures (and watches for suspicious behaviour), then quarantines or deletes infected files.

front: Is a compiler system or application software?
back: System software: it is a translator that converts code into machine code.
Saving stores the working copy; a backup is a second copy on a different device or location, used to restore lost or damaged data.
